rationale: Firecrawl is a production-grade web scraping API with a monorepo containing the core TypeScript API (481 source files in apps/api/src), 8 official SDKs (Python, JS/TS, Go, Rust, Ruby, Java, Elixir, .NET, PHP), and supporting services (Playwright microservice, Go HTML-to-Markdown, Redis, RabbitMQ, PostgreSQL/FDB queue backends). The scraping pipeline implements a sophisticated multi-engine waterfall: fetch → playwright → fire-engine (Chrome CDP, TLS client with stealth modes) → specialized engines (PDF, Wikipedia, X/Twitter, document). Engine forcing allows domain-specific engine selection. Queue infrastructure uses BullMQ/Redis for job scheduling, RabbitMQ for extract jobs with DLQ, and NuQ (PostgreSQL/FDB) for notification queues. LLM-based structured extraction (/extract endpoint) supports JSON Schema with Pydantic/Zod validation. Stealth features include TLS fingerprinting and Chrome CDP stealth modes. Self-healing is achieved through engine fallback waterfall and retry logic. The codebase has 252 test files, Docker Compose for local/prod deployment, and comprehensive self-hosting documentation. Tier A: high architectural depth, multi-language SDKs, production deployment artifacts, and direct relevance to scraping pipeline concerns.
limitations: No formal architecture/ADR documents beyond CLAUDE.md and ENGINE_FORCING.md
Fuzzy matching/dedupe not directly observed in source
Full-text search indexing is present but not a standalone concern
Script generation (LLM-generated scraping scripts) not a native feature
AGPL-3.0 license may constrain commercial embedding
Fire-engine advanced anti-bot features not available in self-hosted version
Supabase required for authentication features in self-hosted
